newsitem.title: USA: Falling gold prices force Echo Bay review.
newsitem.headline: Falling gold prices force Echo Bay review.

text.p: Echo Bay Mines Ltd said Wednesday it is conducting a major review of its gold mines and development projects to determine the carrying values of its assets, in light of both short-term and long-term views of precious metals prices.
The review is expected to be finished in the third quarter.

The average gold price realized by Echo Bay fell by $42 per ounce of gold sold in the second quarter, ended June 30, to $350 per ounce, from $392 a year ago, the company said, but realized prices by the company exceeded world spot prices due to the company's hedging programs.

The company reported a net loss today of $20.7 million, or $0.17 per share in the second quarter, versus a loss of $14.6 million, or $0.11 a share in the year-earlier period, largely because of sharply lower gold prices and the higher costs of processing lower grades of ore.

The company also blamed the drop in gold prices on the the possible deferral of final construction of the Paredones Amarillos gold mine in Mexico, a joint venture with Viceroy Resources Corp, and its New Aquarius mine in Ontario.
Such a deferral would reduce Echo Bay's total 1997 capital spending at the Mexican mine to $10 million, from $44 million, and to $39 million, from $70 million at the Canadian mine.
Echo Bay also said that in July it implemented the final steps of a corporate office downsizing that it expects to produce cost savings of $4 million in expenses in 1998.
